summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of neurogenic bladder, paraplegia, and recurrent urinary tract infections was admitted with a three-day history of fever, nausea, and worsening abdominal and flank pain. She had self-treated with leftover Macrobid prior to admission. In the emergency department, she received IV vancomycin and ceftriaxone. Hospital evaluation confirmed pyelonephritis due to E. coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin. Renal ultrasound showed no hydronephrosis or stones, and lower extremity ultrasound ruled out DVT. Her Foley catheter was changed on admission. By hospital day three, she was afebrile and clinically improved, and transitioned to oral nitrofurantoin for completion of a 14-day course. However, she eloped from the hospital before formal discharge, without collecting her medications or discharge instructions. Efforts to contact her at the number provided were unsuccessful.
